campaign_rulings.summary: Off-duty Sedation locks last through the current Off-Duty period and clear only at its explicit end, surviving pauses and restarts.
campaign_rulings.rationale: A bounded period fits Minor Punishment without inventing permanent treatment; owner accepted the recommendation.
alternatives: Require later treatment to remove the lock

campaign_rulings.summary: Retain the mark and current-period Sedation lock when an embraced Tag replaces a locked Identity or renames its Paired slot; printed explicit removal remains separate.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 17 / printed p.15; Tag replacement PDF 11 and Paired slot PDF 58; delegated owner authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: Replacement must not act as an unprinted extra unmark while Sedation prohibits unmarking during the period.
alternatives: A replacement Identity starts unmarked and unlocked
Prohibit replacement of any locked Identity
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: M2 repeated-Tag embrace and Paired rename retain the slot lock; optional unmark selectors exclude locked Identities.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Apply a revised choice policy only to future events after updating reducers and tests; explicitly migrate pending locks if requested, keeping historical receipts unchanged.

campaign_rulings.summary: A repeated identical chosen track/severity/row/column flags a severity switch at the next Off-Duty start; it does not reroll the saved current event.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 142, 144–145, 147–148, 150–151 / printed pp.140, 142–143, 145–146, 148–149; delegated owner authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: Severity changes occur at a period boundary. Retaining the chosen event avoids an unprinted automatic reroll and preserves immutable receipts.
alternatives: Switch severity immediately and reroll
Switch severity immediately while keeping the event
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: The pure scheduler records a pending repeat flag and consumes it once at the next period start.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Changing timing requires migrating pending repeat flags and queue policy explicitly; preserve past rolls and already selected effects.

campaign_rulings.summary: High result 6 column 2 counts all prior selected occurrences on its own track across the campaign, excluding itself; two or fewer queues one Low and one High roll, otherwise an unused Endgame.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 145, 148, 151 / printed pp.143, 146, 149; delegated owner authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: The text asks how many other events have occurred. Counting persistent occurrences gives a stable auditable threshold and finite recursive escalation.
alternatives: Count only distinct table slots
Count only events in this Off-Duty cycle
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Stable parent-linked recursive requests and Endgame choices survive serialization and transactional history. Specific event effects remain required work.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: A revised counting window affects future threshold checks; preserve already created child requests and explicitly review any changed pending queue.

campaign_rulings.summary: The current DoctorDoctor owner records credit/no-trigger before the Budget start review. High Budget Obsolescence applies once at the resulting starting severity.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 71, 142, 150–151 / printed pp.69, 140, 148–149; delegated owner authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: Resolve the owner's earned credit declaration before an eight-box Budget trigger can scrap the Frame; neither a missing owner nor a replacement invents their answer.
alternatives: Record a deferred pre-scrap credit snapshot
Resolve Budget first and separately migrate any old-frame credit task
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: The preparation service waits for actual owner credit records, marks Obsolescence atomically, and queues context-bound compulsory replacement at eight.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Changing the ordering requires explicit migration of pending old-Frame credit work and origin-bound replacement tasks; do not recalculate historical Permission grants.

campaign_rulings.summary: One square permits any of eight neighbors; Directed steps reduce distance to the actual current goal.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 121–123 / printed pp.119–121; delegated owner authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: The map uses squares and eight surrounding territory squares without an explicit diagonal travel rule.
alternatives: Orthogonal-only movement
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Pure movement validates the Handler-selected adjacent step; world end remains under source-specific period integration.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Revise future legal destinations explicitly; do not move old entities retroactively.

campaign_rulings.summary: Outside a surviving location, an Aggressive Gorgon changes behavior Class while preserving its existing body, Assets/damage, archetype Types, Core and visibility.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 123,165 / printed pp.121,163; delegated owner authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: Aggressive is a Class; interpreting the loose word type as behavior change allows the named escalation without inventing free repairs or deleting Assets.
alternatives: Change the archetype Type instead of behavior Class
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Pure period-end requires an exact Handler choice and validates all preserved state. New-Class counts apply only to creation.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Pending world moves require fresh review if this interpretation changes; preserve historical resources and reveal provenance.

campaign_rulings.summary: Preserve existing Assets/damage, add two intact Assets and a distinct additional Type, and specify the rebuilt unexposed Core conditions. Existing Types remain; Sprite followers inherit current leader Types.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 145,164,166 / printed pp.143,162,164; delegated owner authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: The return result specifies new Assets/Type but not a free refresh or repeated multi-Type fallback; an explicit Core plan preserves the normal exposure procedure.
alternatives: Refresh all old Assets or replace an existing secondary Type
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Typed Strain revival validates the defeated target, exactly two new owned Assets, an additional Type and new Core plan.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Revise future revivals only; do not rewrite defeated incarnations, past damage, or already committed rewards.

campaign_rulings.summary: Reprogram ordinary starting slots to fresh unmarked defaults with the chosen current label in the prescribed/fallback slot; preserve protected extras/Paired identity state and transfer active Sedation restrictions by stable slot. Printed explicit removals remain separate.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 28 / printed p.26; protected/Paired PDF 58; Sedation PDF 17; owner delegated authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: Reset implies the established starting baseline, but cannot erase protected resources or bypass the accepted current-period Sedation replacement restriction.
alternatives: Retain the chosen current card with its old mark while resetting others
Unmark every Identity, including protected/locked resources
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Stable ordinary slot metadata is bound in a real M3 period event without adding/removing resources. New ordinary reset IDs are source-derived; protected/Paired objects retain IDs and marks.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Changing mark semantics affects future resets. Preserve historical outcomes; review pending resets and scoped Sedation locks explicitly rather than rewriting existing receipts.

campaign_rulings.summary: M3 Identities with matching labels remain distinct cards identified by stable IDs/slots; enforce the actual four ordinary/Paired slot cap.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 10 / printed p.8 and PDF 28 / printed p.26; owner delegated authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: Printed reprogramming can retain a current default label while restoring the same default elsewhere. The book does not forbid duplicate labels; merging or rejecting them would change source-owned choices and resource counts.
alternatives: Reject any retained label already in the starting set
Merge matching labels into one card, reducing available Identities
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Trusted M3 policy enables duplicate labels in shared Tag/Paired replacement, core Off-Duty recovery, Correctional Programming and reset. Selection and marking remain ID/slot based; clients cannot choose the policy. Existing M2-only behavior remains unchanged.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: A revised uniqueness policy needs explicit treatment of existing distinct cards and pending choices; never silently merge identities, marks or protected resources.

campaign_rulings.summary: Capture Frame and Queen-holder eligibility at the actual Off-Duty roll; DoctorDoctor keeps the approved pre-Budget start ordering.
campaign_rulings.rationale: The printed trigger does not order later replacement/Court transfers against outstanding choices. Binding actual earned eligibility preserves its owner without restoring old resources.
alternatives: Use the Frame and holder at the later submission time
Freeze all Frame bonuses at period start
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Existing immutable roll-state history is referenced and checked against the action, receipt, character and period. Only current Permissions are changed.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Future ordering changes require explicit pending-work review; do not move earned choices to a new holder or recalculate saved rewards.

campaign_rulings.summary: The normal Frame Off-Duty triggers also apply when Void Observation replaces the ordinary roll.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 28 and Frame Permission triggers PDF 61–88.
campaign_rulings.rationale: Observation replaces rolling Go Off-Duty while retaining Off-Duty recovery and the broader period; it does not expressly suspend Frame triggers.
alternatives: Suspend bonuses during Observation
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: The common Frame reward scheduler now accepts a real, provenance-checked Observation roll. The actual positive JANUS bonus and no-trigger review are tested on that route. Full playbook/world interactions remain pending.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: A revised exclusion affects future Observation periods and outstanding reviews, retaining prior receipts.

campaign_rulings.summary: The Queen holder cannot award itself while it is the Dog; it can choose another current Girl who is the Dog.
campaign_rulings.rationale: The parenthetical Dog restriction is attached to the self-award clause, rather than all recipients.
alternatives: Exclude every Dog recipient
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: The actual Queen holder selects a legal current Girl; self-Dog is rejected server-side.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Review pending recipient selectors after a change; never revoke a completed award silently.

campaign_rulings.summary: A particular character can earn a prisoner bonus only once from one actual custody/delivery record; joint contributors are not globally excluded.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 65 and 78; sheets PDF 19 and 23.
campaign_rulings.rationale: An actual delivery should not be repeatedly re-presented as new, while the text supplies no exclusive single-captor quota.
alternatives: Permit repeat rewards for the same delivery
Allow one bonus total across all contributing characters
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Consumed delivery provenance is recorded per actual character ID. Current delivery-state checks are implemented; complete custody/event-history selection remains pending.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: New pricing/eligibility policy requires explicit treatment of pending delivery claims and preserved consumed-source receipts.

campaign_rulings.summary: Player and Handler choose distinct consequences across the shared Observation list.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 28 / printed p.26; owner delegated authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: Separate choose counts refer to one outcome list; distinct consequences avoid selecting the same surgery or assignment twice without source instructions for stacking.
alternatives: Permit the same consequence once for each human
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: The reducer enforces distinct values within and across saved selections; each human still owns its exact count.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Changes affect legal pending selections and need explicit treatment of already selected/resolved effects; retain dice and completed effects.

campaign_rulings.summary: The affected player chooses the retained current Identity and any approved fallback slot for Observation reprogramming, regardless of who selected that consequence.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 28 / printed p.26; owner delegated authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: The text does not allocate the nested choice. Preserving the affected player's own Identity choice avoids treating non-Punishment reprogramming as the separately ruled inflictor-owned Punishment default.
alternatives: Let the human selecting reprogramming choose its Identity details
Always assign reprogramming details to the Handler
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: A separate affected-player request applies the actual reset reducer and preserves protected/locked slots.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: A new owner rule requires reassignment of pending requests; do not reset already settled Identities or impersonate an absent player.

campaign_rulings.summary: The Handler plays the general populace for its actual public-display Tag and is recorded as that Tag's human giver.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 28 / printed p.26; owner delegated authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: The source specifies the populace as giver but supplies no separate player role; the existing core Tag system identifies the human controller.
alternatives: Invite another explicit human to play the populace
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Public-display Tag detail is a separate Handler-owned request. Harpy Candidate uses its printed fixed label; neither is automatically marked.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Changing controller representation affects future Tag authority and pending choices, and requires an explicit migration for existing giver provenance.

campaign_rulings.summary: Overlapping Directors share one continuous Handler Girl-rules episode; additional arrivals do not restart Heat or grant another starting Identity set.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 192 / printed p.190; owner delegated authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: The source defines a state while in the Director's presence, without stacking/reset rules for several Directors. One continuous context preserves its actual resources.
alternatives: Reset Heat and replace the Identities for every arriving Director
Create simultaneous independent Girl sheets
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: The actual Handler selects two ordinary starting cards once; later overlapping presence binds its own source work to the existing context. The Handler stays outside the Pilot roster.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: A change needs explicit treatment of active contexts and pending work; never reset spent Heat or duplicate existing cards silently.

campaign_rulings.summary: The final actual Director departure ends this rule authority without unmarking cards, granting Heat or restoring an older Heat balance. A later new presence starts its printed zero-Heat/two-Identity context.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 192 / printed p.190; owner delegated authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: The source specifies the start but no exit recovery or resource restoration. Preserving actual resources prevents an inferred free recovery or banked reset.
alternatives: Restore the Handler's earlier Heat balance
Discard all Heat immediately on departure
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Departure is an actual separately owned human action. Context history and resource marks remain private canonical evidence; no timeout ends it. Shared Girl Play integration remains pending.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Revised exit behavior affects future episodes and active-context review, preserving prior receipts and actual resource changes.

campaign_rulings.summary: Use a human different from the current Handler to play the Director throughout this campaign.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 151 / printed p.149 explicitly requires another human for High Budget 1/1; PDF 188–189 permits broad NPC control and PDF 192 defines Director rules.
campaign_rulings.rationale: Generalizing the explicit High Budget separation keeps the opposed Director/Handler roles and their actual decisions distinct. This is a campaign recommendation, not a universal restriction printed in the generic NPC rules.
alternatives: Require a different human only for High Budget 1/1 and allow self-play in other Director scenes
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: NPC introductions, invitations, claims and Observation presence enforce the trusted implemented separation. A Director may still be played by a Girl player; roles must stay distinct from their Pilot identity.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Relaxing the global default needs actual scene-specific actor binding and tests so the explicit High Budget requirement remains enforced. Preserve existing role/control and response provenance.

campaign_rulings.summary: The current informed Handler explicitly records each actual breach and chooses whether its separate Punishment is due in the current actual mission/Off-Duty context or the next Off-Duty period.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 17 / printed p.15; Moderate consultation PDF 18 / printed p.16; owner delegated authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: The source permits concealed behavioural rules and requires further Punishment on breach, but does not define automated detection or a reporting procedure. Human adjudication preserves fictional knowledge and the printed now-or-later discipline timing.
alternatives: The original inflictor adjudicates all later breaches
Require the affected player to confirm each breach
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: No passive chat ingestion, automatic judgment or inferred player response. A concealed rule remains private to its actual author and informed Handler. Every recorded occurrence has its own source event and discipline cause; next-period deferral does not become current-period work.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Changing the adjudicator or timing requires explicit knowledge/authority migration and treatment of pending breach causes, without replaying a Punishment or disclosing a concealed rule.

campaign_rulings.summary: A Low Budget 4/2 shortage rolled during Off-Duty binds to the next actual dispatched mission, then the actual recovery period following that mission. Do not retroactively restrict the already-ended mission or the current recovery.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 150 / printed p.148; owner delegated authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: The source says after the next or current mission. The implemented Off-Duty lifecycle starts only after actual missions finish, so a new event has no active current mission to bind. Actual dispatch/end events provide a stable next-mission anchor without guessing fictional time.
alternatives: Treat the mission preceding this Off-Duty as current and restrict this recovery immediately
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Preserve each actual source event. Bind all unanchored shortages on the next real dispatch, then its end and the following actual period. Overlapping one-Asset limits do not grant additional free quotas. Extra paid repairs still use explicit current Handler quotes and owner confirmation.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Changing the interpretation needs explicit migration of unanchored/mission-bound restrictions and pending quotes. Preserve prior recovery and payment receipts; never retroactively charge or damage an Asset.

campaign_rulings.summary: The current-period missed-supply -2 applies to the selected Girl's actual Off-Duty roll, including Void Observation when it replaces Go Off-Duty.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 150 / printed p.148 and PDF 28 / printed p.26; owner delegated authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: The loss concerns this recovery period, while Observation replaces the ordinary roll. Carrying the same pre-roll consequence through the replacement avoids erasing an already assigned loss by switching routes.
alternatives: Apply the -2 only to ordinary Go Off-Duty and omit it under Void Observation
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Use the actual complete character-bound Cadre population and one OS-backed uniform draw. Preserve assignment and source event. Apply once before dice/Tags and retain separate base/supply/Tag modifiers, receipt, restart and generation ownership.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Revising this interpretation needs treatment of unrolled Observation reservations and assigned losses. Never alter known dice/tier receipts, redraw a committed recipient or apply the effect to a new character.

campaign_rulings.summary: The current Handler represents the Foundation scientific demand and explicitly selects one or two actual Girls, with a separate explicit hiding-suspicion review for each.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 150 / printed p.148 and PDF 28 / printed p.26; owner delegated authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: The event specifies one or two Girls but no player-facing selection procedure. The current Handler adjudicates the event as a Foundation demand, without inventing a Girl response or consent.
alternatives: Ask the Cadre to choose volunteers
Use a random draw for the scientists targets
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Validate distinct actual character/period targets and exact yes/no suspicion answers. Apply real source-bound Observation orders, preserving all owed recovery; this grants no transport, medical help or NPC role acceptance.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: A revised selection owner needs its actual owned request and pending-order migration. Preserve known selections, character incarnations, receipts and separately answered humans.

campaign_rulings.summary: Scientific demand overlapping an existing same-period Observation keeps one actual roll with distinct recorded causes; it does not roll or lower Status twice.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 150 / printed p.148 and PDF 28 / printed p.26; owner delegated authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: Observation replaces the period recovery roll, and the scientific event can require it even without another cause. The source does not require an extra independent recovery cycle for an already observed Girl.
alternatives: Require separate additional Observation rolls and consequences
Disallow selecting a Girl already under Observation
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Preserve original context/source and append a distinct real scientific cause. Before any reservation or human choice, the Handler records a fresh explicit hiding review. Actual Observation completion fulfills the bound causes once.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Changing overlap behavior needs treatment of unrolled orders and owed causes. Never duplicate a known roll/Status loss, overwrite prior human responses or silently discard provenance.

campaign_rulings.summary: A currently controlled, explicitly cast Director supplies Handler-rule replies to the actual Handler acting under Girl rules. OOC scene facilitation remains separate.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 192 / printed p.190; owner delegated authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: The Director uses Handler rules while the physical Handler uses Girl rules. Keeping the two roles distinct prevents self-adjudication or granting the Director player global GM knowledge.
alternatives: Keep every Handler-rule reply assigned to the original OOC facilitator
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Director offers its actual cast role. The acting Handler confirms that Director when reserving a Play. Persist both actual actor references and controllers, and revalidate current presence and control on every response.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Changed adjudication needs explicit recovery of outstanding decisions with preserved receipts and prior owned answers; no silent controller transfer.

campaign_rulings.summary: When mixed-role Tag proposals compete, the adjudicator proposes one actual proposal and all scene humans explicitly agree before its modifier applies. A rejection returns to discussion.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 11 / printed p.9; owner delegated authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: The source permits discussion as an alternative to Status or rock-paper-scissors. Unanimous recorded discussion handles roles outside Pilot Status without inventing NPC, Harpy or Director ranks.
alternatives: Use the printed expanded Status hierarchy with explicit current fictional exceptions
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: One response per real human, not per controlled character. Only other humans may propose a Girl Tag, through one actual cast role. Preserve the original proposals and never infer agreement from timeout or silence.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: A revised dispute procedure needs explicit pending-proposal migration and source-correct actual actor ranks. Preserve applied modifiers and already recorded human decisions.

campaign_rulings.summary: Creature Comforts waits for an actual future ordinary Go Off-Duty roll of 8 or more after post-roll modifiers. Void Observation does not consume that opportunity.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 16 / printed p.14; PDF 28 / printed p.26; owner delegated authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: The source expressly names rolling 8+ to Go Off-Duty. Observation has its own replacement Play and result table, so retaining the paid benefit until the named roll preserves that trigger.
alternatives: Treat an 8+ Void Observation replacement as qualifying too
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Use actual raw-roll state to prove the purchase existed before dice, the actual final receipt/action and original character. Low rolls and Observation leave the paid purchase waiting; a queued opportunity requires the owners actual scene or explicit decline.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Changing this interpretation needs review of waiting purchases and unfinished opportunities. Preserve known qualifying receipts, actual scenes, paid costs, granted Assets and human decisions.

campaign_rulings.summary: Each separately paid Creature Comforts purchase has one optional opportunity on its next actual qualifying ordinary Go Off-Duty roll. Multiple paid purchases may qualify on the same roll.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 16 / printed p.14; PDF 28 / printed p.26; owner delegated authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: Each receipt pays for its own future benefit. The text gives no limit of one outstanding purchase or one benefit irrespective of how many Permissions were paid. Asset limits still apply to every actual grant.
alternatives: Limit the player to one pending purchase or one opportunity per recovery period
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Bind each immutable paid source once to one real roll and one owned improvement scene. Never multiply an unpaid source; each granted Asset records its purchase and remains subject to the Girl Asset cap and non-Void replacement rule.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: A new stacking limit must address already paid waiting purchases explicitly, without deleting costs, fabricating refunds or reusing known rolls for extra grants.

campaign_rulings.summary: Declining the optional Creature Comforts scene at its actual next qualifying roll consumes that paid opportunity without refund; it grants no Asset or scene.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 16 / printed p.14; owner delegated authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: The purchase pays for an opportunity at the next named qualifying roll, and the scene is optional. The source provides no refund or repeated opportunity after an explicit decline. Silence still leaves the decision pending.
alternatives: Keep an unused paid benefit waiting for a later qualifying roll
Refund a declined optional scene
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Disclose the cost and no-refund consequence before the owner confirms decline. Preserve the original cost, qualification and explicit owned decision. Never infer decline from absent humans or a timer.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: A different campaign interpretation needs explicit treatment of declined opportunities, preserving their real costs and decisions. Do not fabricate refunds or retroactively grant Assets.

campaign_rulings.summary: A destroyed original designated Gorgon guard satisfies the Asset condition for Core exposure. The actual recorded conversational weakness must still be fulfilled and explicitly confirmed.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 162, 164 / printed pp.160, 162; delegated owner authority.
campaign_rulings.rationale: Destruction removes the actual guarding Asset rather than restoring protection or leaving an impossible requirement to damage an Asset that no longer exists. Preserve the independent weakness condition and actual Core destruction for death.
alternatives: Require a new explicit Core-plan review after every designated guard destruction.
Treat destruction as insufficient until the table resolves a different means of fulfilling the Asset condition.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Keep destroyed actual Assets as immutable canonical history outside usable Assets. Original Core/protection references retain provenance; destruction never automatically exposes or kills the Gorgon.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Review existing pending Core exposures and actual destruction sources before changing this interpretation. Preserve historical Asset destruction and confirmed Core outcomes; do not resurrect an Asset or reroll a known result.

campaign_rulings.summary: Benevolent Gorgons cannot initiate Attack or Collateral Damage, but can defend when another Gorgon pits Assets against them. The Handler chooses the actual contest winner.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 162, 167 / printed pp.160, 165; delegated owner authority.
campaign_rulings.rationale: The Attack rule explicitly includes a Gorgon target and a Handler-chosen Asset contest. The Benevolent restriction forbids initiating its attack, without requiring it to lose an opponent-initiated contest; a defensive result can follow from the attacker striking its protection.
alternatives: Require Benevolent Gorgons always to lose or avoid any Asset contest.
Permit defense but require a separate bespoke defensive outcome rather than the printed contest.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Reject Benevolent initiators in both NPC and Gorgon Attack commands. Permit it only as the actual defender of another Gorgon, with the actual Handler winner and chosen losing pitted Asset.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Review pending defensive contests when changing this ruling. Preserve prior actual winner decisions and destroyed-Asset history rather than silently undoing consequences.

campaign_rulings.summary: Every unconsumed Low Rebellion 1/2 occurrence adds its own +2 to the next actual Girl Disobey Orders roll; that one roll consumes all waiting occurrences.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 147 / printed p.145; delegated owner authority
campaign_rulings.rationale: Each occurrence refers to the next actual refusal, without a non-stacking limit or permission to postpone one occurrence to a later roll.
alternatives: Consume only one queued +2 per refusal.
Treat repeated occurrences as a single non-stacking +2.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Keep distinct source works/events and consume every waiting bonus atomically with the actual receipt. Heat and later Tag adjustments remain separate.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Review unrolled reservations and waiting occurrences before changing the interpretation. Preserve known dice, original receipts and consumed sources; do not silently refund, reuse or postpone a recorded bonus.

campaign_rulings.summary: For Put Someone Beneath You, the effect chooser selects the printed effect, while the affected Girl owns selection of their private Bond endpoint or counter-damaged Asset. Explicit Tag selection stays with the printed chooser; Punishment details retain the inflictor-owned ruling.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 22 / printed p.20; owner delegated future recommendations in this conversation
campaign_rulings.rationale: The source assigns effect choices but does not explicitly assign private Bond/Asset details. Keep the actual affected human responsible for those details without disclosing their private sheet or NPC relationships to another player.
alternatives: Let the effect chooser select every resource, exposing the required target details.
Use an explicit table-negotiated resource choice for every instance.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Review unfinished private-detail requests explicitly; preserve known dice, effect choices and already applied outcomes. Do not change Punishment choice ownership or fabricate player consent.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Freeze the chooser-owned printed effect, then request the affected original character owner to supply its actual private Bond or undamaged Asset. Retain the same receipt and apply the effects atomically only after the owned detail response.

campaign_rulings.summary: The inflictor states a restoration condition for a temporarily removed actual Requisition, then confirms when it is met. The affected original owner restores the resource, selecting any required legal Asset replacement.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF 16–17 / printed pp.14–15; owner delegated future recommendations
campaign_rulings.rationale: The printed temporary removal has no duration or restoration owner. Preserve the original resource and receipt, with an explicit reversible condition rather than inventing a fixed number of scenes.
alternatives: Automatic restoration at the next Off-Duty period.
Handler chooses duration and restoration even when another Girl inflicted it.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Supported paid Asset Installment temporarily removes its actual Asset, preserving ID, damage, Void state and original Frame. A pending Creature Comforts benefit cannot qualify or grant while suspended. Consumed benefits cannot be revoked. Restoration gives no refund, repair, duplicate reward or replacement Frame; future Requisition types need their own actual suspension effects.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Change only unresolved conditions prospectively with an explicit superseding ruling; preserve paid receipts, suspended originals and recorded restoration decisions.

campaign_rulings.summary: Handler creation uses original-appointment/persona-bound owned shared starting proposals. The affected original Girls accept or decline shared history, Bond, rank and printed Trainer starting phrases. Private Handler details remain private. Late initial activation preserves any already stronger M2 Bond and moves selected Ace/Dog while preserving other relative order.
campaign_rulings.rationale: The book assigns starting selections but does not specify digital agreement ownership, late initialization over accepted M2 resources, or custom versus printed Bond-story selection. Shared exact owned proposals protect human history choices without revealing Handler background/playbook/gear. Already stronger canonical relationships must not silently downgrade during initial M3 persona creation.
alternatives: Apply starting Bonds/ranks directly without shared-history agreements.
Set every starting Bond to the exact printed depth, downgrading accepted stronger M2 relationships.
Require printed histories exclusively, without custom human-authored histories.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Use trusted handler_creation=owned_shared_choices_preserve_existing. Starting stories may be human-authored or selected prompts; only selected Trainer printed stories automatically install their named phrase sets. Insurgent selects1–2 actual living Handler NPC Bonds Surveilled and1 actual living NPC Bond Sympathizer; overlap is allowed because the source does not say the labels are exclusive. Gear descriptions create no extra NPCs, vehicles, map movement or surveillance. Canonical persona identity is distinct from account and appointment event; old forms cannot reactivate or overwrite it.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Change future creation proposals prospectively. Existing accepted source-bound proposals, canonical initial effects, current relationships and private draft history require explicit review before reinterpretation; do not reset M2 resources or fabricate another human response.

campaign_rulings.summary: Actual medical waking clears only confirmed incapacity/vitals; the original Girl then owns an available Girl Play exchange from a currently unused base Girl book.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF29 / printed p.27; delegated recommendations
campaign_rulings.rationale: The injury option names waking and an unused playbook but gives no digital medical confirmation or definition of unused. Actual current native playbooks define use without treating a borrowed single rule as an extra character class. Care evidence and waking remain explicit human facts.
alternatives: Treat borrowed rules as occupying their entire source playbook.
Immediately wake the Girl or repair all resources automatically.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Original patient proposes actual help; current appointed Handler confirms that exact source context. Recovery preserves placement, vessel, custody and damaged Assets. Explicit restored vital signs are separate from waking. Original CID owns the subsequent swap. Only fully implemented acquisitions are selectable; other actual rule IDs remain runtime_pending, with no synthetic acknowledgment resolver.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Changing unused-book semantics affects future offers; existing acquired ownership remains source-bound. Changing care authority requires review of pending exact proposals; do not retroactively fabricate medical help or consent.

campaign_rulings.summary: Changing the whole Girl playbook establishes a new native baseline and preserves still-owned explicit third-party acquisitions and sourced setup; prior swap masks are archived with their old epoch.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF29 / printed p.27; delegated recommendation
campaign_rulings.rationale: The low Defeat result changes the Girl book but does not direct loss of separately acquired Plays. Old masks apply to the old baseline and must not suppress a newly provided native rule. Boolean rule ownership avoids granting duplicate effects when a prior acquisition is now native.
alternatives: Discard all previously acquired rules on any Girl playbook change.
Keep old removal masks active against the new native baseline.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: change_playbook_runtime returns a new sheet and source fact containing prior runtime. retained_rules plus current swaps determine ownership; native and acquired instances never stack the same rule. Existing protected identities and distinct body/frame resources remain caller-owned responsibilities. Required new-book stateful setup stays real required work.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Any different retention rule needs explicit review of existing acquisitions and affected pending setup. Preserve previous epoch facts rather than rewriting swap history.

campaign_rulings.summary: Acquired To a Higher Standard uses the same three original human choosers as native ownership: self, one actual bonded other Girl, and the currently appointed Handler.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF32 / printed p.30; Defeat PDF29 / printed p.27; delegated recommendation
campaign_rulings.rationale: A never-Princess borrower lacks native draft setup. Applying the printed chooser instructions to the actual acquiring Girl preserves original human authority without changing class, copying stale draft choices or leaving a nominal nonfunctional capability.
alternatives: Give the borrower default standards chosen by the bot.
Reject this otherwise implemented acquisition forever when native draft labels differ.
Apply the rule before the original other choosers respond.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Source-bound private standards work stores each actual original choice/event independently. Missing chooser stays pending; owner may withdraw/restart with current real participants. Medical acquisition compiles all three choices and atomically activates them with the actual rule exchange. A new native baseline can invoke the same setup independently. Handler standard counts as an order. Mission-end trigger and review follow current rule ownership, so removed native rules stop and borrowed rules work. Preserve explicit after-promotion Ace Permission plus normal Ace bonus.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Chooser/consent changes invalidate only affected pending exact proposals; do not transfer another human response across CIDs or Handler appointments. Existing native accepted M2 standards remain reusable; runtime ownership is distinct from private draft class labels.

campaign_rulings.summary: A full Girl book change retains the original body and actual resources and configures only newly active continuous-rule requirements; it does not rerun character creation.
campaign_rulings.rationale: Defeat says change the Girl playbook, without resetting Identities, purchasing new Assets, advancing rank or introducing new NPCs. Continuous rules still need actual owned choices, and their source authority must follow original people rather than account labels.
alternatives: Recreate the entire Girl and supply two free starting Assets, new Bonds and initial Ace rank.
Change only the class label and leave stateful native rules unusable.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Create original-CID/new-baseline required work immediately after the actual Defeat event. Newgirl requires current Handler assignment and actual Mentor callsign; Bonded requires nominated original Pair acceptance and owner selection of the existing Paired slot or one ordinary slot renamed Hers. Preserve protected extras and existing Paired protection; install Personal/Intense depth without Heat rewards or weakening a stronger Bond. Oldgen chooses two maxims. Princess uses actual three-chooser standards without a new-game Ace reset. Vatgrown names its actual DNA basis, chooses desires for retained actual starting NPC investors, and the current Handler chooses their own desires. Casualty initializes nine typed parts only if no prior parts exist, preserving prior damage. AM and Mockingbird retain actual bodies, Identities, limiter/protected evidence and Assets; no extra body, limiter reset or automatic Void corruption. Native unimplemented Plays remain fail-closed independently.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Change prospective setup requirements only after reviewing current pending choices and original CID/epoch. Do not invent human responses, heal old damage, downgrade Bonds or overwrite another person’s protected Identity. Source review is still required for the printed omission.

campaign_rulings.summary: First creation describes the existing Handler; actual existing relationship graph edges adopt that first persona. Later persona replacements preserve old source identities and gain no inherited authority.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF124/printed122; delegated digital identity clarification
campaign_rulings.rationale: M2 already has actual Handler relationships before a named M3 persona exists. Treating first persona creation as a new person would silently orphan valid Bonds; treating every later persona as the same person would transfer authority across replacements.
alternatives: Discard all pre-persona Bonds on first persona creation.
Transfer every prior persona relationship to each future replacement automatically.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: First activation migrates actual legacy Handler(None) edges, installs the actual first persona, rebinds those edges to its actual persona ID and sets printed starting depths through the single actor graph. Already stronger Bonds are preserved. Only legacy Tags lacking both giver_actor and giver_character receive an explicit first-persona binding; already bound setter evidence remains unchanged. Replacement personas migrate old graph before replacement and never rebind it to the new person.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Any alternative identity model requires explicit graph/Tag-source review before applying to a populated campaign; preserve old original-person evidence and do not mint replacement consent.

campaign_rulings.summary: Privacy binds the first actual Off-Duty activation after payment; an already-active-period purchase waits for the next activation. Either ordinary or Void Observation is permitted.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF16 and27–28 / printed14 and25–26; delegated recommendation
campaign_rulings.rationale: Privacy says next off-duty without a roll8+ condition; Observation is an alternate off-duty route. Freeze actual activation-state paid sources and original characters.
alternatives: Bind only ordinary Go Off-Duty.
Permit an already-active interval retroactively.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Actual period activation state must contain the paid original receipt; no late purchase claims a known activation. Companion original CID remains bound.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Review outstanding period-bound benefits before adjusting timing; preserve paid receipts and consumed outcomes.

campaign_rulings.summary: The original buyer may decline an unused qualified optional scene without refund; no timer or Handler acknowledgment chooses for them.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF16 / printed14; existing Comforts decline recommendation applied to scene benefits
campaign_rulings.rationale: Printed benefits are optional paid opportunities, not refundable currency exchanges or mandatory invented scenes.
alternatives: Refund unused benefits.
Carry qualified opportunities to another period.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Record actual owned decline; qualified requests remain pending until their actual owned scene or decline.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Preserve prior payment and decisions; explicitly review unfinished qualified requests.

campaign_rulings.summary: Either original participant may explicitly end Privacy pause-safe. Actual original career endings terminate protection without fabricated consent, while old scene audience remains private.
campaign_rulings.rationale: No interruptions protects the two Girls against outsiders; it does not force continued human participation or let delayed delivery publish old scene details.
alternatives: Require both participants to approve ending.
Let Handler or timers end protection.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Owned end records no automatic travel. A career end records actual archive/ended ActorRef rather than pretending voluntary close consent. Closed scene IDs require fresh public scene identity; proven existing continuations may resolve privately.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Preserve original audience and known rolls; never retroactively expose earlier scene text.

campaign_rulings.summary: Visiting Home uses an actual Foundation-affiliated supervising role, whose human owns agreement before actual co-travel. Ordinary Go Off-Duty8+ qualifies; Observation does not.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF16 / printed14; delegated recommendation for supervision detail
campaign_rulings.rationale: The benefit is Foundation-supervised; source does not name a required supervisor playbook or add approval/payment. Use actual Controller/ActorRef and actual Foundation affiliation, not invented NPCs.
alternatives: Require current Handler personally.
Let arbitrary unknown actors supervise.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Actual current Foundation Pilot/Handler or canonical Foundation-employed/affiliated NPC/external Pilot can supervise. The body and supervisor co-travel offstage and return via source-proved physical journey, preserving original positions and injuries.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Review unfinished supervision agreements if eligibility changes; never transfer old consent to a new controller/body.

campaign_rulings.summary: After actual death/execution in active Privacy, current Handler chooses actual inquiry or supported Punishment. The original survivor owns response/refusal; with none, Handler records concrete method/question/report and known/unknown evidence.
campaign_rulings.rationale: The book promises trouble without specifying a mandatory Punishment. Require actual human-authored consequence and preserve secret prior-room content rather than inventing guilt or disclosure.
alternatives: Always inflict Punishment.
Allow a generic handled checkbox.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Actual investigation creates typed question/method and surviving original human reply/refusal, explicitly shared with Handler. No survivor uses actual Handler-authored investigation report, with no manufactured NPC or witness. Punishment routes to real discipline work and effects.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Preserve actual recorded questions/responses, private room audience and original character binding; review unfinished source-linked consequence explicitly.

campaign_rulings.summary: A new character on the same Discord account has a fresh gameplay incarnation; the predecessor's immutable sheet, resources and relationships remain original-character history.
campaign_rulings.rationale: Printed compulsory new-character outcomes require an actual new Girl. Reusing an account or stable SQL profile must not transfer the previous Girl's authority or rewards.
alternatives: Delete the original sheet and receipts
Reuse the account's old canonical identity and resources
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Canonical IncarnationBinding separates gameplay CID from stable SQL profile and receipt FK. Fresh creation starts empty progress and requires explicit Handler starting Status. Actual archived participation remains source readable.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Different lifecycle identity policy would require an explicit audited data migration; ordinary accounts never acquire old authority automatically.

campaign_rulings.summary: A one-Girl roster is both actual Ace and actual Dog; Ace takes precedence for the single numeric Status modifier. Empty rosters have neither role.
campaign_rulings.source: rulebook Status and mission-position benefits/consequences; PDF 14 / printed 12
campaign_rulings.rationale: Preserves the actual highest and lowest positions after genuine career endings without inventing another Pilot or blocking survivors forever.
alternatives: Block all mission completion until a second Girl is activated
Apply only one of the two printed position consequences
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Current Ace receives genuine Ace benefit; the one survivor also receives Dog consequence. Departed original participation never rewards or punishes a replacement by UID.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Changes affect future one-Girl mission benefits and Status rolls; original mission records remain immutable.

campaign_rulings.summary: An imprisoned Girl may resume after an actual Handler offer and her original human owner's choice. If another Girl is active, preserve her in an immutable reserve archive rather than overwriting her.
campaign_rulings.source: rulebook PDF 18 / printed 16 explicitly allows Handler-authorized return; active-account coordination is a campaign implementation ruling
campaign_rulings.rationale: Allows the printed return while avoiding two canonical Girls sharing UID-only controls, disappearing replacement resources, or forged owner choice.
alternatives: Never permit the printed return
Silently overwrite the replacement
Allow simultaneous same-account Girl control before all workflows support multiple originals
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Explicit return Status is bound to the exact other-original roster. Keep saved resources without healing, invented location or new piloting consent. Resolve the current Girl's actual obligations, Helplessness, custody, journey, mission, Off-Duty and protected-scene commitments before switching. Only imprisonment and explicitly reserved originals are eligible; death, Execution, Retirement and Harpy conversion do not resurrect.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: A future multi-character account UI could replace reserve switching, but must preserve source CIDs and old obligations.

campaign_rulings.summary: Career ending alone does not erase all historical Bonds. Preserve exact original ActorRef edges; their controller's replacement receives none of them.
campaign_rulings.source: rulebook PDF 13 / printed 11 and explicit Bond-removal effect PDF 196 / printed 194
campaign_rulings.rationale: The source explicitly specifies all-Bond erasure for Lobotomy; inventing universal erasure on death or imprisonment would add an unsupported effect. Conversely account IDs are not fictional people.
alternatives: Erase every Bond on every career ending
Transfer Bonds to a replacement controlled by the same human
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Typed graph migrates each legacy numeric/NPC edge to one source-bound authority; zero-depth tombstones prevent fallback. Above-Intense Heat goes only to actual live resource owners, including the distinct Harpy port, never another controlled actor. Source conversion may explicitly rebind the same fictional person to her Harpy body.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Future erasure or weakening applies through actual original endpoints and preserves prior audit; historical actors do not acquire replacement Heat.

campaign_rulings.summary: Lobotomy resets ordinary starting Identity slots, erases the inflictor's two eligible slots, preserves explicitly protected Identities, and uses the normal ordinary four-slot cap for an implanted Identity.
campaign_rulings.source: rulebook PDF 196 / printed 194 together with the actual protected-Identity and ordinary-cap rules
campaign_rulings.rationale: A broad reset should not silently override a printed protection; implantation does not state a cap exception. Stable slots preserve Sedation marking rather than granting an unrelated unmark.
alternatives: Erase protected extras and protected Paired slots
Treat the implant as an unlimited fifth ordinary Identity
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Inflictor chooses unspecified details under the explicit owner ruling. The reset-then-erase option has exactly two eligible ordinary slots removed; new memory has a described Identity, with an eligible replacement only when still at cap. Existing protected extras and surviving locked slots retain their actual protections/marks.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Changing this interaction affects future surgeries; already applied surgeries remain source records and require explicit correction rather than recalculation.

campaign_rulings.summary: Experimental surgery remains a pending Punishment until the actual inflictor selects one to three effects and details, the actual original patient supplies all printed descriptions, and the inflictor completes those saved effects.
campaign_rulings.rationale: The text assigns the selections to the surgeon and descriptions to the patient. Generated dialogue or a generic acknowledgement cannot stand in for the patient's actual contribution.
alternatives: Generate the patient's responses
Resolve the Punishment immediately at type selection
Apply separate partial effects before a recoverable original source exists
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Source-owned canonical Surgery records preserve all phases and actual participant ActorRefs; no surgery preparation or patient description spends resources or resolves discipline. Actual application is atomic with original debt and bundled causes. Blank name is a source-proved state and clears the Discord nickname via the existing cosmetic queue. Blocked Plays retain actual surgery provenance, including mandatory Plays; the source-specific mandatory no-roll adjudication rule is owned separately by root.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Alternative staging must preserve existing patient-authored descriptions, source effects and all unresolved original obligations.

campaign_rulings.summary: The current human of a represented Core voices it; an unrepresented ordinary NPC Frame is voiced by the current Handler.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF24/printed22 and PDF68/printed66; digital control clarification
campaign_rulings.rationale: The source requires consent without naming the human for each ordinary Frame. A represented Core has its own actual identity.
alternatives: Let the Pilot consent for the Frame.
Let the Handler override represented Cores.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Use controller_or_handler. A dead or captured represented Core does not transfer authority. Consent is original subject and Frame bound, one use; opening, extraction and healing remain separate actual operations.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Review unfinished exact consent requests before changing authority; preserve original bodies, injuries and source histories.

campaign_rulings.summary: A surviving Girl with a Frame destroyed by Defeat proposes its different free replacement during preparation of the next actual Off-Duty period.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF29/printed27; explicit owner different Frame, free charge and Handler-defined package decisions
campaign_rulings.rationale: The source says next time off-duty without defining a software phase. Real period preparation permits the new Frame before required scenes while preserving delayed source ownership.
alternatives: Replace immediately in battle.
Delay the package until after the period roll.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Transfer the original obligation to a new actual period task with immutable original Frame proof. Handler quotes the exact free package, player confirms, external Court recipient consents. Preserve Girl resources and factual old placement.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Review outstanding destroyed-Frame obligations before changing timing. Never grant duplicate packages or rewrite saved source histories.

campaign_rulings.summary: Every post-death Handler is a fresh source-bound persona. Insurgent may propose Personal starting Bonds to selected actual living known NPCs; their actual controllers explicitly accept the exact shared history, including when the Handler and NPC share one human. No old body Bond transfers or invented NPCs.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF135 / printed p.133; seven printed Handler starting packages; owner delegated recommendations and source-owned original-body preservation
campaign_rulings.rationale: The Insurgent selects NPC Bonds without specifying digital establishment or post-death replacement relationships. A prospective persona ID and global body-generation token separate the new original from the GM account and appointment. Exact controller agreement makes the printed starting package usable without transferring archived relationships or silently accepting another role.
alternatives: Require prior established new-persona NPC Bonds before creation, leaving new Insurgents unable to start.
Reuse dead Handler NPC relationships by account ID.
Spawn NPCs or establish relationships without actual controller agreement.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Only an initial persona with no Handler archives globally may adopt existing legacy Handler(None) relationships. Later creation is generation-bound to the latest global Handler archive source event. Old saved or unsaved forms and old persona IDs cannot activate a replacement. Selected Surveilled and Sympathizer labels may overlap; one shared relationship is proposed per actual NPC. Creation creates no transport, NPCs or vehicles.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Apply changes prospectively to new proposals. Preserve archived originals, accepted source events, historical Tag setters and explicit human decisions; changing defaults must not rebind historical Bonds.

campaign_rulings.summary: If actual experimental surgery removes the ability to roll a mandatory Defeat, Go Off-Duty or Void Observation Play, keep the inability and await an explicit current Handler decision assigning its complete integer total before actual Tag choices.
campaign_rulings.source: rulebook PDF 18 / printed 16; PDF 27–29 / printed 25–27; PDF 196 / printed 194. The resolution of this conflict is a campaign ruling, not an explicitly printed exception.
campaign_rulings.rationale: Preserves both the actual prohibition and the source-mandated consequence without manufacturing dice, restoring the removed ability, generating a favorable result, or permanently deadlocking the campaign.
alternatives: Leave mandatory consequences permanently blocked
Restore the forbidden ability without a source
Automatically choose a favorable outcome or invent dice faces
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: The actual original prohibition is proved against its completed surgery event. The mandatory source is proved against pending original Defeat work/response or the actual original's active Off-Duty period. Freeze Handler persona and original CID; only that actual human Handler supplies an integer and factual reason. The whole pre-Tag total is assigned without RNG, dice faces, Heat/Identity spending, numeric base additions or consumption of next-roll supply bonuses. Keep Void Observation's genuine Status-demotion effect. Normal actual Tag choices and owned downstream outcomes follow. Mark receipts MANUAL ADJUDICATION with the source decision. Voluntary forbidden Plays remain blocked, and no ability is restored.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Changing this conflict resolution affects future mandatory adjudications. Existing manual receipts, source prohibitions, actual Handler decisions and resulting owned choices remain immutable audit evidence. Replacing a Handler or original character requires explicit source recovery rather than moving authority to a new person.

campaign_rulings.summary: High Dive Deep preserves each printed chooser independently: the Girl chooses one effect and the actual Handler chooses one; the same option may be chosen twice and must apply legally twice.
campaign_rulings.rationale: The text gives separate choices but does not prohibit overlap or specify asynchronous digital consequence order. Real table effects must finish before irreversible Void conversion can remove their original recipient.
alternatives: Require different effects even though the source does not state distinctness.
Permit a first conversion to delete the original character before the second selected effect is applied.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Actor then Handler each supplies one source-bound option. Apply both original resource effects and real table responses, then lower Status exactly once for the synchronicity spike and open all real Void thresholds while retaining the root lock. Every repeated effect uses then-current actual resources and a distinct actual source event. External Void overlap semantics remain owned by that subsystem.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Changing order or overlap changes pending exact choices and downstream snapshots; review existing original action/step facts before any migration, never reroll or rewrite old human decisions.

campaign_rulings.summary: Dive table decisions belong to the frozen actual source cast controllers plus explicitly joined OOC facilitator, deduplicated by actual human controller.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF24/printed22; source cast rules; delegated recommendation
campaign_rulings.rationale: The book says the table answers or decides but does not specify a Discord voting protocol. Every original human must retain an actual choice, and one human controlling two roles does not become two independent voters.
alternatives: Let the bot or Handler automatically answer for absent humans.
Count each fictional role as a separate table vote.
Apply a majority decision over an explicitly rejecting original human.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Each actual table human answers an owned question request. For a replacement Identity, the actual Handler coordinates a concrete ordinary-slot/new-label proposal; every frozen human accepts or rejects that exact revision. Rejection requires a new proposal and discards old approvals. Protected extras/Paired slots remain protected in this ordinary-Identity workflow. Full escaped source questions/proposals are paged privately before response. NPC-controller Tag modifier ownership is a separate source-role integration, not inferred from controller UID.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Changing table membership or approval semantics affects pending original requests. Do not transfer a response across CIDs, Controller roles or Handler appointments, and do not synthesize approval for a missing human.

campaign_rulings.summary: Affected original Girl owns Asset rewrite/ordinary Identity details; the actual Handler owns each nearby NPC manifestation. An effect must have actual applicable source resources or context.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF24/printed22; Void PDF19–20/printed17–18; delegated recommendation
campaign_rulings.rationale: The source assigns option selection but leaves digital detail ownership and nearby distance unspecified. A descriptive empty outcome must not stand in for missing mechanics, and known actual co-presence must not create movement or extra NPCs.
alternatives: Let the option selector overwrite every private recipient detail.
Invent a fixed numerical radius or new nearby NPCs.
Record empty-target radiation as completed NPC corruption.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: The original Girl chooses its actual uncorrupted Asset and rewrite or actual ordinary Identity and question. For NPC radiation, affect every living NPC proven same actual cell or actual frozen cast co-presence; the Handler chooses one of four printed manifestations for each. Require at least one actual NPC, an actual ordinary Identity for identity effects, or actual own-cockpit occupancy for subsumption; fail before RNG if no option can apply. Frame Plays remain legal outside the Frame otherwise. Mockingbird Risk Factor uses actual own occupancy, including inside_frame without piloting, and current rule ownership.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Changing proximity/detail ownership requires prospective selector changes and review of pending source choices. Existing positions, protected Identities, Asset damage and source NPCs must not be reset or invented.

campaign_rulings.summary: A Tag marker selects one actual original controlled role; Bond bonuses use that ActorRef rather than its Discord controller ID.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF11/printed9; Personal/Intense Bond rules; explicit owner ±2 ruling; delegated digital interpretation
campaign_rulings.rationale: One human can control a Girl and NPC or several NPCs. Numeric NPC IDs and controller accounts are distinct namespaces, so their relationships cannot be substituted for each other.
alternatives: Use the controller UID for every NPC Bond modifier.
Let a second controlled role bypass the rolling human’s printed self-mark restrictions.
Require an extra visible selector even when only one actual role exists.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Freeze original source cast roles/controllers and actual facilitator. Native multiple-role windows require an explicit role picker; a single proved role remains implicit for existing Game.respond callers and is invisibly hash-bound in native UI. Validate the actual original role, resource hash and graph Bond depth/bonus; unknown or changed roles fail closed. Original Girl self-mark exceptions remain required and a second owned NPC cannot proxy them. Reopen only the actual stale human proposal, preserving dice and committed Heat. Store applied ActorRef/source hash privately; do not expose hidden user-named NPC IDs through generic public modifiers.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Changing role selection or bonus ownership affects pending exact proposals. Review original cast/controller/ActorRef and graph evidence; never adopt controller Bonds, transfer character authority, reroll dice or infer another human response.

campaign_rulings.summary: When competing Tag proposals include a role with no printed Girl Status, actual original table humans resolve the choice through explicit unanimous discussion without a numeric Status surrogate.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF11/printed9; prior scene_unanimous_discussion ruling; delegated native protocol
campaign_rulings.rationale: The source permits Status, discussion or rock-paper-scissors. NPC/controller UID ranking would fabricate Status, while automatically accepting the coordinator’s proposal would manufacture a human vote.
alternatives: Treat NPC controllers as their own Girls for Status priority.
Let a coordinator decide for all humans.
Reveal every private Tag/relevance or hidden NPC name to the entire table.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Keep existing Status priority for actual ranked Pilot/Handler-only proposals. Mixed non-Status proposals use actual coordinator selection followed by every frozen table human’s own acceptance/rejection, including coordinator. Rejection discards old approvals before a new exact candidate. Non-witnesses see only a masked proposal/modifier; Tag label and relevance stay with original witnesses and affected owner, hidden role names stay with controllers or revealed roles. Page full escaped owned text before native agreement. Apply one actual Tag once, only after current source validation and actual discussion; source graph changes invalidate the original bonus snapshot.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Changing discussion or privacy semantics requires reviewing pending original-source proposals and approvals. Never add observers automatically, synthesize votes, expose unrelated private sheets or use stale approval for a different source actor/bonus.

campaign_rulings.summary: The original human GM can continue the printed other-player Tag window after their fictional Handler dies. An explicit OOC marker has no fictional body, Bond bonus or Status priority and can grant only the ordinary one-point modifier.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF11 / printed p.9; actual Handler body-ending rule; delegated original-persona protocol
campaign_rulings.rationale: The human GM and their fictional Handler are distinct. A body ending must archive its original Bonds and authority without stranding the same original table human in Pass or discussion controls. Using a new Handler persona would transfer original authority.
alternatives: Require a new persona before the human GM can Pass.
Use the dead body or new persona Bonds and Status.
Allow only Pass and omit the printed other-player Tag option.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Use Marker.actor=null with enforced depth0/bonus1. For legacy windows prove the original GM body from the actual Play-confirmed event and canonical history. For mixed contexts preserve the exact frozen table/facilitator and accept only the original archive-proven Handler role removal; arbitrary cast changes remain stale. A later persona never replaces the old source role. Competing OOC/role proposals use explicit actual-human discussion without Status ranking; observed-Tag privacy and self-mark restrictions stay in force.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Review pending exact role snapshots and actual source body endings before changing this protocol. Preserve original roll/Heat, graph history, human votes and private Tag witnesses.

campaign_rulings.summary: Temporarily revoked, earned but unspent Requisition benefits leave the old period's scheduling as deferred, then transfer to a real active period after original inflictor confirmation and original owner restoration. They are never marked consumed or declined by that transfer.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF17 / printed15 temporary Revoked Privileges; PDF16 / printed14 Requisitions; delegated recommendation
campaign_rulings.rationale: A restoration condition such as next mission would otherwise permanently block the current Off-Duty period or force forfeiture of a paid benefit. Deferral preserves both the temporary condition and original payment/earned roll without creating currency or rerolling known dice.
alternatives: Block the original period until restoration, which can deadlock a next-mission condition.
Force permanent paid-benefit decline to progress.
Waive the original inflictor condition automatically.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Append-only old work resolution requisition_temporarily_suspended then requisition_benefit_transferred; new actual period work retains original purchase, actor CID, raw roll, action and total plus restoration source. Clear incomplete old scene consent; retain actual fully attested Creature Comforts scene. No new benefit to replacement characters. Personal Firearm restores same confiscated actual item, or only entitlement if already lost; original Frame/grant remains mandatory.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Review outstanding deferred and transferred work before changing scheduling. Never retroactively treat transfer as actual consumption, decline, refund or a new qualifying roll.

campaign_rulings.summary: A paid optional Frame Swap selects a different official Frame playbook, uses its normal two chosen starting Assets and printed setup/extras, and retains exactly one actual old Frame Asset plus one actually unlocked old Frame rule. It costs four Permissions and never uses the compulsory replacement package.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF16 / printed14, destination starting playbooks PDF61/65/68/71/74/78/81/84/88; delegated recommendation
campaign_rulings.rationale: New Frame Playbook supplies its normal starting baseline; the printed retained Asset and rule are the additional explicit carryover. Existing Girl resources and actual item ownership do not disappear because her assigned machine changes.
alternatives: Permit repeated exchange into the same playbook.
Treat retained items as the entire new baseline rather than additional carryover.
Use the compulsory Handler-defined free replacement package for a paid swap.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Price4 at final atomic owner payment after actual new Frame delivery at the unchanged body location. Exact original Court recipient must accept. New CONSUME Quiet/Doctor0 use already approved campaign defaults. New Changeling strings bind actual existing Bond counterparts. Old Frame is source-archived parked, never fake-scrapped. Actual Girl pistol remains the same item; retained Firearm rule transfers future lost-item entitlement without reissue. Wyvern Enormous's extra-cap treatment is a native base rule, not silently carried with the Asset alone. Already completed historical exchange is not revocable currency or a reversible time operation; selectors expose only currently held removable benefits. Unimplemented/review-pending native baselines and retained-rule consumers remain gated.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Changing baseline/retention requires reviewing actual existing new Frames, paid receipts and parked old Frames; no automatic charge/refund, item duplication or context rewrite.

campaign_rulings.summary: An Enforcer's NPC superior-officer exception uses an explicit current Handler factual rank declaration relative to the original Girl. Foundation detention persists until actual current Handler evidence establishes innocence; ending the accuser's career does not erase Foundation custody.
campaign_rulings.source: Book PDF78 / printed76 Obedience Conditioning; delegated implementation interpretation
campaign_rulings.rationale: NPC playbook jobs do not establish military rank. The printed arrest is a real custody consequence, not proof of objective guilt or forced belief by the Handler. Releasing custody does not establish where the original body physically is.
alternatives: Assume all NPCs except Directors are subordinate.
Let the accuser choose whether the target is superior and when innocence is established.
Restore the NPC to a stale map location automatically.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Original rank/accusation ActorRefs and actual state/event proofs. Detained NPC may participate in actual prison roleplay; only unsupported escape/movement is blocked. Current cell unknown through custody and after release until one concrete sourceful factual map declaration. No new prison coordinate, counterfactual extraction or timer. Production full Obedience gate remains closed until trust/volunteer consumers and independent review actually complete.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Review outstanding actual NPC custody and source-bound cases before changing rank or innocence authority; preserve original evidence and do not move bodies as a policy side effect.

campaign_rulings.summary: When full Girl and Frame corruption are pending together, retain both exact sources, resolve actual Frame enclosure first, and preserve full-Girl allure after a real escape.
campaign_rulings.rationale: The book gives both conditions without a simultaneous-effect order. A successful printed escape must not erase the remaining corruption or duplicate the same physical body.
alternatives: Require completed Harpy transformation before allowing the Frame escape.
Create independent competing physical transformations.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Consumers: engine.m3_void.start_threshold, services.m3_void.prepare_threshold, services.m3_physical.PhysicalService.operate. Scope: implemented_under_delegation. This interpretation does not enable missing consumers.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: One actual damaging escape and one original Frame Gorgon; Girl remains her original body/resources. Canonical allure persists, and actual entry into a future assigned Frame opens a new source-backed threshold.

campaign_rulings.summary: If the Girl is actually outside her affected Frame, do not enclose, move or damage her to manufacture an escape. The Handler gives the actual original Frame its Gorgon form at its existing known or unknown position.
campaign_rulings.rationale: Basic Frame Plays explicitly work outside the Frame, while the corruption paragraph assumes enclosure. Preserving the separate actual body and applying Frame transformation is the least added effect.
alternatives: Defer all Frame transformation until actual entry.
Charge an escape injury even though she was never enclosed.
campaign_rulings.implementation_note: Consumers: engine.m3_void.abandoned_frame, engine.m3_void.confirm_occupancy, discord_adapter.m3_void.open_void. Scope: implemented_under_delegation. This interpretation does not enable missing consumers.
campaign_rulings.change_impact: Original Girl position, vessel, injuries and resources stay unchanged; actual Frame Assets retain identities/damage in the Gorgon. Unknown occupancy first receives owned factual proposal plus independent Handler confirmation.
